articles.title: Rhinos and elephants can cause huge problems if reintroduced badly—here's how to get it right
articles.description: Moving large animals around is a seductive idea in conservation. If there are plenty of animals in one place and too few in another, moving some between the two seems an obvious solution. Sometimes it is. But with animals as large, mobile and socially complicated as elephants and rhinos, the move itself can turn out to be the straightforward part.

articles.title: Quantum interactions may have locked early universe's fields into existing energy states
articles.description: The universe may be trapped in its own comfort zone, and a researcher in the College of Engineering and Computer Science has helped explain why it cannot seem to leave. A new study suggests the universe could be locked into its current state by the same kinds of quantum effects that scientists study when trying to preserve fragile information inside a quantum computer.

articles.title: Testing Whisky in Space Using an Artificial Tongue Could Help Explore Foundations for Orbital Factories
articles.description: Learn about an upcoming project that will distill whisky in space, uncovering chemical changes to lay the groundwork for orbital factories.

articles.title: Optogenetics wins the Nobel – one neuroscience breakthrough in a line of technological innovations helping scientists map and control the brain
articles.description: Neuroscientific advances follow a pattern of visualizing the brain, measuring its function and then controlling it. Optogenetics may lead to a new era of medical treatment.

articles.title: Australians continue to embrace solar, but is everyone benefitting equally?
articles.description: Household solar is transforming Australia's energy system, but UNSW expert Associate Professor Anna Bruce says there is a challenge to make sure the advantages are equitable.

articles.title: Creatine May Help Middle-Aged Adults Maintain Strength Without a Structured Workout Routine

articles.description: Learn how an unexplained illness prompted hospital quarantines in Siberia and why reports of a plague ingestion remain unconfirmed.

articles.title: Rare insect discovery reveals a new species from the dinosaur age
articles.description: Some 99 million years ago, during the age of the dinosaurs, a tiny insect belonging to a species previously unknown to science became trapped in tree resin. The resin hardened and turned into amber, and the fossil preserved within it has now enabled a team of researchers from the School of Zoology and The Steinhardt Museum of Natural History to identify and describe a new species: Cretodorus noonoo, or "Noo-Noo."

articles.title: How psychopathic traits shape language
articles.description: Popular culture often depicts people with psychopathy as cold, emotionless and hollow, but a recent University of Mississippi study found that the language associated with psychopathic traits is more complicated than often described.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ Australians report higher rates of psychological distress, national survey finds
articles.description: A Monash University study analyzed data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics' 2020–2022 National Study of Mental Health and Wellbeing and found more than half of cisgender nonheterosexual Australians and more than one-third of transgender Australians are diagnosed with a mental disorder.

articles.description: Three scientists won the 2026 Nobel Medicine Prize for pioneering optogenetics, a light-based technique that transformed brain research and neuroscience.

articles.description: Vaxcyte said its experimental pneumococcal vaccine hit the primary endpoints in a Phase 3 clinical trial, setting up the biotech to compete with Pfizer and Merck.

articles.description: Using data from the Japan-led XRISM observatory, astronomers have directly observed a giant star’s stellar wind captured by its compact companion (triggering X-ray flares) for the first time.

articles.title: ‘When I saw the video I cringed’: Why CNN anchor says to stop analyzing kids’ sports on the ride home
articles.description: CNN anchor Don Riddell details how the "drive home" has become a dreaded rite of passage for young athletes trapped in a vehicle while emotions are raw. He explains what researchers recommend instead of an immediate critique.

articles.title: Nanoneedle arrays map RNA in fresh tissue without sequencing or amplification
articles.description: Recently, spatial omics has become a powerful tool, enabling researchers to see not only what molecules are present in a tissue, but also where they are located and how they are organized across cells, tissue structures and local microenvironments. This spatial context has deepened our understanding of cancer, neurobiology and immunology. Yet as the field advances, an important question remains: How many of these powerful technologies are ready for routine clinical use?

articles.title: Informal businesses belong in entrepreneurial ecosystems, review argues
articles.description: A systematic review of informal businesses published in the International Journal of Entrepreneurship and Small Business argues that they should be treated as part of the larger entrepreneurial ecosystem rather than as a peripheral feature of the economy.

articles.description: If you've ever felt overwhelmed by menu options at a restaurant, cereal varieties at the grocery store or potential partners while scrolling through dating apps, you've experienced choice overload.

articles.title: Gamma-ray search sets new limits on dark matter annihilation in the inner Milky Way
articles.description: Dark matter could be a type of matter in the universe that does not emit, absorb or reflect detectable light and appears to interact very weakly with regular matter. Although physicists have observed gravitational effects attributed to dark matter, they have not yet been able to determine what it is made of.

articles.title: Taste shapes support for climate-friendly school meals
articles.description: Students in a new study were neither clearly positive nor negative about more climate-friendly school meals. Whether the food tasted good, was filling and felt familiar played an important role. Students were somewhat more positive about reducing the amount of meat in recipes than about having more all-vegetarian days.

articles.description: MacSync malware hides malicious commands inside iCloud calendar events to download additional payloads onto infected Macs without raising suspicion.

articles.description: We tested 12 top-rated leaf blowers to compare their performance, ease of use, battery life and design. Two models stood out as the best choice for most people.

articles.description: The U.S. prison population is declining at an accelerating rate, and prison admission rates are predicted to fall an additional 50% within the next two decades, according to new research from University at Albany professor Shawn Bushway.

articles.title: Inka scattered sacred coca leaves over sacrificed llamas, excavation suggests
articles.description: Deep in Peru's Acarí Valley lie the ruins of Tambo Viejo, an Inka provincial center where excavations have uncovered tasseled sacrificial llamas and brightly adorned guinea pigs. But save for a few seeds and some stored leaves, evidence of how the Inka used one of their most sacred plants in rituals remained elusive. Now, archaeologists have discovered coca leaves still stuck in the wool of some sacrificed llamas.
